newsitem.title: USA: Muni groups seek White House aid on yield burning.
newsitem.headline: Muni groups seek White House aid on yield burning.

text.p: Seven state and local government groups are asking a presidential panel of top U.S. financial regulators to oversee the federal government's response to "yield burning," an official with one of the groups said.

William Pound, executive director of the National Conference of State Legislatures, said his and six other groups are asking Marcia Hale, a special assistant to President Clinton, to have the President's Working Group on Financial Markets respond to the issue.
Chaired by Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin, the group includes the heads of the Federal Reserve Board, the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission.
It was formed by a presidential executive order in March 1988 following the October 1987 stock market crash.
The muni groups, known as the "Group of Seven," met with Donald Lubick, Treasury's assistant secretary, on January 27 with recommendations on yield burning, but they have received no response.
Yield burning refers to allegations that bond underwriters overcharge states and localities for U.S. Treasury securities they bought to help them refinance their outstanding bonds.
The Internal Revenue Service has told municipalities that they can avoid having bonds declared taxable by settling any overcharges with the agency now.
But muni groups told Lubick in January that the vast majority of localities were unaware of any yield burning and that the SEC's enforcement staff, not IRS, should take the lead on the issue.
Pound said on Tuesday that muni groups met with Hale about 10 days ago on the issue and "this is a followup (letter) to indicate our concern on the matter."
"It asks that the interagency task force be brought in (to) examine the thing," Pound said.
Such a move could be awkward for Treasury Secretary Rubin who already has recused himself from any decisionmaking on yield because of a possible conflict of interest.
